text:
San Jose arrives in Dallas on the second night of a back-to-back, winless in four (0-4-0) and outscored 18-5 in that run after a 4-1 loss at Minnesota last night. The Sharks are without Igor Chernyshov and Alexander Wennberg, and Michael Misa has taken on more minutes. Dallas, two days removed from a shootout loss at Columbus, is missing Miro Heiskanen, with Thomas Harley moving onto the first power-play unit. The Stars won the Oct 5 meeting 5-0.

The numbers favor Dallas. At five on five, the Stars have taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in their games, while San Jose sits at 44%, and our model projects 3.5 expected goals for Dallas against 2.53 for the Sharks. Dallas also allows far fewer on the penalty kill, 0.53 expected goals a game to San Jose's 0.99, and the Sharks take 4.2 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Jake Oettinger is +7.6 goals saved above expected this season, against +4.7 for Alex Nedeljkovic, who was at -2.06 last year.

Wyatt Johnston and Jason Robertson are both at 40% to score, and Mikko Rantanen is at 77% for a point after reaching 800 career points, as Tom Gulitti of NHL.com posted. For San Jose, Macklin Celebrini is 74% for a point. Our under-the-radar pick is Tyler Seguin, a third-liner with 2.8 expected goals over his last 10 games, at 23% to score. We also like Harley for a point (46%) against the league's leakiest defense in chance quality.
